What does Bergamot Essential Oil smell like?

Sparkling, sweet-tart citrus with a distinctive floral-lavender and slightly spicy tea-like nuance, more refined than other citrus oils. The backbone of colognes and fougeres; perfumers use it generously in top notes to lend elegance and lift.

Use Bergamot Essential Oil in a formula

How do you use Bergamot Essential Oil in a perfume?

Read from this material's catalog record and PerfuMate's published formulas.

  • It is a top note: it shapes the opening of a perfume, the first minutes to hours, and fades before the heart and base do. On a blotter it lasts about 8.0 hours.
  • Its impact is 6 of 10: medium. Trial it at a modest share first and raise it on the strip rather than by guess.
  • In 6 published formulas, most of them accords, it makes up 2% to 35.7% of the concentrate (median 12.5%). An accord is one part of a perfume, so expect a smaller share in a finished formula.
  • Weigh it neat, or from a 10% dilution when you need small amounts; both are common on the bench. The free dilution calculator does the arithmetic.
  • In the published formulas it sits most often beside Hedione, Habanolide, Vertofix Coeur and Beta-Ionone.
  • It is restricted under IFRA, and how much is allowed depends on the finished product and its strength. Check a formula with Bergamot Essential Oil in the free IFRA calculator before anyone wears it.
